clue.text: With time running out, injured party institutes court proceedings

indicators.note: injured means damaged or hurt, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
time running out means a T for time leaves the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A wronged party, short of time, starts legal action in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With time running out' removes one T from PARTY INSTITUTES; 'injured' then rearranges the fourteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawsuits brought to establish who fathered a child are a familiar kind of legal action.

clue.text: Perhaps midwife's instrument that's potentially harmful if taken?

parts.note: the midwife toad is a species of toad, so 'midwife's' is an example of a toad's, signalled by 'Perhaps'
a tool is an instrument or implement

explanation.surface: A question about whether a midwife's equipment might be dangerous to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwife' reads as the birth attendant, but it is the midwife toad, a European amphibian whose male carries the eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Many fungi of this kind are poisonous, so eating one can do serious harm.

clue.text: Bore pompously referred to home

definitions.meaning: an archaic past tense of abide, meaning endured or put up with
a grand, rather stuffy word for the place where one lives

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an old past tense of abide (bore, tolerated) and a formal noun for a dwelling.

clue.text: Martial arts expert returns full of excellent spirit in spring

indicators.note: full of means one piece is filled with another, so letters go inside
returns signals that the word for the martial arts expert is read backwards

parts.note: a dan is a grade of black belt in judo or karate, hence an expert
A1 (written AI) means first-class or excellent

explanation.surface: A karate black belt comes back brimming with fine spirit for the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the expert's grade into NAD, and 'full of' fills it with the A1 rating; 'spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph who lives in a spring, river or fountain.

clue.text: Medication taken before solid food at teatime?

indicators.note: taken before places the medication word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: drops are a form of medicine, for eyes or ears
a cone is a solid geometric figure

explanation.surface: Advice to take one's medicine before eating something substantial at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A drop scone is a small thick pancake, a traditional British teatime treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone (Scotch pancake) is a small griddle cake served at afternoon tea.

clue.text: Industrial fluid laced with one for printers as far as I know

indicators.note: laced with means having something mixed in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: meths is methylated spirit, an industrial alcohol
ink is something printers need

explanation.surface: Some industrial liquid has been spiked with something for printers, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic phrase meaning it seems to me, close in sense to as far as I know.

clue.text: Agent putting forward quiet, superb dwelling

indicators.note: putting forward means moving one letter of the agent word to the front

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
fab is informal for fabulous or superb

explanation.surface: An estate agent keeps his voice down while pushing a wonderful house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting forward' moves the P of REP to the front, giving PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house, especially the temporary homes built in Britain after the Second World War.

clue.text: Retiring Greek character within was first to drive away

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole construction is read in reverse
within places the Greek letter inside the other word

parts.note: led means was in front, was first
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A shy Greek who was first inside goes off to drive away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' and 'Retiring' together give LEPSID read backwards; 'Greek character' looks like a person but is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts or fears is to drive them off or banish them.

clue.text: Cheers after veteran nurses scrap bad blood

indicators.note: after places the thanks word at the end
nurses means holds or cradles, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an end is a leftover scrap, as in odds and ends
ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Thanks given after an old soldier tends a fight that caused ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and TA are both casual British ways of saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud, a state of lasting enmity.

clue.text: Classic author surely, once, eclipsing those in front

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering or obscuring, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: certes is an archaic word for certainly or surely
the van (vanguard) is those at the front

explanation.surface: A classic writer was once sure of overshadowing his predecessors.
explanation.definitionFit: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, a classic of Spanish literature.

clue.text: Related to solid young reporter in command

parts.note: a cub is a novice journalist
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A junior journalist takes charge in some solid way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic describes three-dimensional shapes and measures, as in cubic metres of volume.

clue.text: What rings have a lot?

parts.note: a ring is a closed loop with no finishing point, and the phrase for that also means a great deal

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a great deal, matching 'a lot', while circles literally lack a finishing point.

clue.text: Bugsy Malone's early years?

parts.note: Bugsy Malone is a film with gangsters played entirely by children, so its title figure is a youthful mobster

explanation.walkthrough: Bugsy Malone (1976) is a musical in which all the gangsters are child actors.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of being a child, one's early years; split it to find a young gangster.

clue.text: Lament Heath's parting in a few words imprudently

indicators.note: parting means dividing, so the lament and the name split the word for briefly

parts.note: to put something shortly is to put it briefly
to sigh is to lament or grieve
Ted Heath was a British Conservative prime minister of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A sad farewell to a politician, put briefly and without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was UK prime minister 1970-74; 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without looking ahead, failing to foresee consequences, is acting unwisely.

clue.text: Remedy, one taken from case by oriental doctor?

indicators.note: taken from means the numeral is removed from the case word

parts.note: a doctor's case is a patient
I is the Roman numeral one
a medic is a doctor
oriental means in the East, read as IN plus E for east

explanation.surface: A cure, one of many supplied to a patient by a doctor from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental doctor' splits as MEDIC + IN E, a doctor in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietary cure-all sold without prescription is a kind of remedy.

clue.text: Imperialist races retaining traditional long clothing

indicators.note: retaining means holding, so the garments go inside

parts.note: the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
saris are long draped garments worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: An empire builder's races keep the old long dress.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (Tourist Trophy) races are run on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Russian emperors, so a supporter of imperial rule.

clue.text: Frames of brass beds taken out and flattened

indicators.note: the frames of the words are their outer letters, and these are what get removed
taken out means the frames are dropped, leaving the inner letters

explanation.surface: The frames of brass beds were removed and squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rased is a variant spelling of razed, meaning levelled to the ground.

clue.text: Press extremely derisive about British military leader

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters go around the abbreviation
extremely picks the extreme letters of the following word

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British

explanation.surface: The press is extremely scornful of a British general.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke is the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Wellington, the soldier who defeated Napoleon.

clue.text: Fearful shot lofted, not very wide

indicators.note: not here means one letter is used instead of another
lofted means sent upwards, so in a down entry the shot word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a volley is a shot in tennis or football
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A shot hit high, and not very wide of the target, from a cricket report.
explanation.walkthrough: VOLLEY upwards gives YELLOV; 'not very, wide' replaces V with W. A wide is a cricket extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, so fearful in that sense.

clue.text: Diffident danseur in production's holding us up

indicators.note: holding means one piece encloses the other
in production means being put together or staged, so the letters are rearranged
up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A shy male ballet dancer is supporting the rest of us in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in production's' gives UNASRED and 'up' gives SU, which 'holding' keeps; a danseur is a male ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking confidence or self-assurance, as a diffident person does.

clue.text: Made a mockery of Left

definitions.meaning: departed, as a plane leaves the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both impersonated mockingly and departed or flew away.

clue.text: Cameramen involved with Derby, a great annual occasion

indicators.note: involved means entangled or mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: TV crews film the Derby, one of the big events of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual day in November commemorating the war dead is a major national occasion.

clue.text: National flower that's lost in Irish borders

indicators.note: borders means surrounds on both sides, so the abbreviation goes around
that's lost means the flower has dropped the following word

parts.note: the celandine is a yellow wild flower

explanation.surface: A citizen whose flower has gone missing within the Irish frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's lost' leaves CELANDE and 'borders' wraps it; 'National' is a noun here, a citizen, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Iceland is a national of that country.

clue.text: On the way out, having fired current missile

indicators.note: having fired means having dismissed, so a letter is sacked from the word

parts.note: perishing means dying, on the way out
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A doomed weapon that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pershing was a US Army ballistic missile of the Cold War.

clue.text: Shriek from native Canadian going into school

indicators.note: going into puts the people's name inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada

explanation.surface: A scream from a First Nations pupil arriving at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a loud piercing cry, just like a shriek.

clue.text: Pop idol following account in paper

indicators.note: following places the rearranged word after the account word

parts.note: a tab is a bill or account, as at a bar

indicators.note: pop means burst or go off, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pop idol following his account in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper of small format.

clue.text: Keeps flowers

definitions.meaning: has in store or carries for sale
scented garden plants of the genus Matthiola

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for holding as stock and the name of a fragrant garden flower.

clue.text: Young trainee hack ignoring judge in court

indicators.note: in places the trimmed horse word inside the court abbreviation
ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a jade is a worn-out horse, a hack

explanation.surface: A young recruit, a reporter, avoids the judge in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist but is an old horse, a JADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.
